newsitem.title: USA: Criticare Systems sets rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Criticare Systems sets rights plan.

text.p: Criticare Systems Inc said Thursday its board of directors declared a distribution of one preferred stock purchase right for each outstanding share of Criticare Systems Inc common stock outstanding on April 24.
"The rights are designed to assure that all shareholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of a potential takeover," Criticare Chairman Gerhard Von der Ruhr said in a news release.
Criticare also said that it had retained investment bankers Robertson Stephens & Co to advise the company.
Criticare officials were not available to elaborate on the hiring of Robertson Stephens, or whether the rights plan was in response to a specific takeover attempt.

The rights, which will expire in 10 years, will entitle shareholders to buy one one-hundredth of a share of preferred stock at an exercise price of $25, but only if a person or group acquires 20 percent or more of Criticare common stock or announces a tender offer which would result in ownership of 30 percent or more of the common stock, the patient monitoring systems maker said.

If Criticare is acquired via merger or other business combination, the holder of each right would then be entitled to purchase $50 market value of the acquirer's stock for $25. The rights also provide for protection against self-dealing and other transactions by a 20 percent shareholder deemed not to be in the best interests of the remaining shareholders, Criticare said.
Criticare shares were unchanged at 4-7/8 Thursday.
